stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model released under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and is optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Google’s next Genie AI model generates more realistic experiences
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Google unveiled Genie 4, a new world model designed for generating interactive AI experiences.
Key features include generating more realistic worlds and enabling real-time updates via natural language prompts.
The model integrates Gemini 3.8 Flash and possesses audio generation capabilities.

stories.title: Code-execution flaw in UEFI firmware threatens most servers on planet Earth
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: A critical code-execution flaw has been discovered in UEFI firmware, specifically within EDK2.
The vulnerability allows attackers to execute malicious code very early in the system boot process.
The flaw poses a significant threat to a vast majority of servers globally.

stories.title: Vibe genes? Natural(ish) language comes to protein, genome design software
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: New AI/genome design software allows users to specify desired protein characteristics using natural language.
This represents a significant step toward intuitive, high-level control over complex biological design processes.
The integration of natural language processing into protein engineering marks a major advancement in synthetic biology tooling.

stories.title: DeepMind unveils Genie 4 world model promising more realistic physics and humans
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: DeepMind has unveiled Genie 4, a new world model.
The model promises significant improvements in simulating realistic physics and human behavior.
It will be made available soon to developers and Google AI Ultra subscribers.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on the Hugging Face platform.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors, indicating a focus on practical LLM deployment.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of Meta-Llama-3-8B on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under key NLP/ML tags such as 'transformers', 'llama', and 'text-generation'.
This indicates ongoing community interest and performance tracking for a major open-source LLM.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically designed for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is optimized to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing private and persistent AI operation.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Anthropic’s elaborate plan to keep Wall Street at bay
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: Anthropic is preparing for an IPO while balancing the need for public market capital with its mission of safe AI development.
The company faces inherent tension between maximizing shareholder returns and mitigating the increased risks associated with more powerful AI models.
The story highlights the ongoing industry debate regarding the commercialization versus the safety focus in advanced AI.

stories.title: Meta’s $25 billion legal loss just put blood in the water
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: Meta faces a massive $25 billion legal penalty following a ruling by a New Mexico judge.
This ruling significantly exceeds a prior $17 billion settlement reached with US attorneys general.
The lawsuit centers on claims that Meta misled users regarding its platform around 2018.

stories.title: Retriever-Free Retrieval: Navigating Documents with Decision Models
stories.author: Kilian Q. Weinberger
bullet_points: Addresses a critical limitation in current LLM architectures: the dependency on external retrievers (lexical/embedding matching).
Introduces 'DecisionRAG,' a novel approach that integrates language model capabilities directly into the retrieval process.
Achieves retrieval evaluation using decision models in a single forward pass, eliminating the need for token generation during the retrieval phase.

stories.title: Reva: Real-Time Vulnerability Detection through Contextual Probing of Large Language Models
stories.author: Massih-Reza Amini
bullet_points: Introduces 'Reva,' a system for real-time vulnerability detection in generated code.
Leverages Large Language Models (LLMs) to act as security experts, performing contextual probing and analysis.
Addresses the growing gap between fast code generation by AI agents and slow human review processes.

stories.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
stories.author: Shyamal Buch
bullet_points: Introduces Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) to bridge the gap between world understanding and robotic action.
Leverages a large pretrained vision-language model (27B parameters) for initial task comprehension.
Uses simulation-based fine-tuning (SFT and GRPO) to teach the model the necessary low-level robotic control.

stories.title: Pretraining Knows What, Simulation Teaches How: Compositional Generalization in a Sim-Trained Robot Agent
stories.author: Shyamal Buch
bullet_points: Introduces Zero-real Agent Policy (ZAP) to bridge the gap between world understanding and robotic action.
Leverages a large pretrained vision-language model (27B parameters) for initial world reasoning.
Uses simulation-based fine-tuning (supervised fine-tuning and GRPO) to teach the model physical control.

stories.title: 155 responses leaked between AI customers: the GLM-5.3 KV cache bug — and the canary test for YOUR provider
stories.author: slabb
bullet_points: A critical data leak was discovered on Cloudflare Workers AI involving GLM-5.3 responses.
The vulnerability stemmed from a stale KV-cache bug, causing responses from one customer to leak data from another.
The article details the technical mechanism and provides a canary test script for users to check their own AI provider's security.

stories.title: Speech models in Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has expanded its capabilities to include support for speech models.
The initial integration features Phonon from Gradium, enabling text-to-speech in five languages.
Performance is highlighted as being over 100x faster than real-time when running on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Clef, a 27B multimodal decision model from Cloudflare, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud infrastructure.
This integration expands the capabilities of Ollama by adding a powerful multimodal model.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now accessible via Ollama.
Beam is specifically engineered for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is offered for free for a limited promotional period through Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
Integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure, deployable AI agent environments.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to questions, choices, and scoring requests.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI services with local, open-weight model ecosystems.

stories.title: Researchers are getting tired of OpenAI gatekeeping its breakthroughs
stories.author: Robert Hart
bullet_points: OpenAI recently announced significant breakthroughs across mathematics, computer science, and physics.
Despite an apparent change in communication strategy, external researchers remain critical of OpenAI's practices.
The article highlights growing frustration among the research community regarding OpenAI's perceived 'gatekeeping' of its findings.

stories.title: Firefox’s Smart Window adds AI form filling and webpage monitoring
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Firefox is enhancing its Smart Window feature with new AI capabilities.
The update allows the browser to auto-fill online forms by pulling data from open tabs.
Examples include using information from LinkedIn or a portfolio to populate job applications.

stories.title: Google begins certifying Registered App Stores for Android, but not in the US
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Google is initiating a certification process for third-party Android app stores.
This move aims to facilitate easier app installations via alternative stores.
The certification program is currently not being implemented in the United States.

stories.title: Ford simplifies using your EV as a home battery with the $30K Fathom
stories.author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
bullet_points: Ford's new Fathom pickup simplifies home energy integration by eliminating the need for a separate wall-mounted inverter.
The vehicle is capable of outputting 10 kW of power directly to a residence.
This feature positions the EV as a viable, integrated home battery storage solution.

stories.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces FLORE, a new framework for learning force-reactive locomotion and manipulation in humanoids.
Addresses the challenge that everyday tasks require controlling contact forces, which kinematics alone cannot specify.
Utilizes robot-free demonstrations captured via force-sensing grippers and wearable body trackers.

stories.title: Patient-specific rubric-based evaluation of large language models across longitudinal cancer care
stories.author: Ying Sun
bullet_points: Introduces NPC-RubricBench, a new phase-aware benchmark for evaluating LLMs in longitudinal cancer care.
Addresses a gap in current LLM evaluations by moving beyond isolated clinical encounters to track care across a continuum.
Uses real-world longitudinal records from 405 patients with nasopharyngeal carcinoma for rigorous testing.

stories.title: I-HITL: Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop
stories.author: Ari Juels
bullet_points: Addresses the growing vulnerability of traditional Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) systems against advanced AI agents.
Introduces the concept of Inalienable Human-in-the-Loop (I-HITL) to enforce strict human approval for AI actions.
The I-HITL protocol ensures an agent cannot initiate critical actions without explicit human consent, even in complex system interactions.

stories.title: Profiling a Frontier Agent with EBench: From Direct Control to Harness with Policy
stories.author: Chunhua Shen
bullet_points: The research evaluates frontier multimodal large language models (MLLMs), specifically GPT-6-Astra, for robot control.
It addresses the gap in comparing MLLM capabilities against established vision-language-action (VLA) and world action model (WAM) policies.
The evaluation is conducted using EBench under a standardized visual and proprioceptive observation protocol.

stories.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Addresses the inefficiency in Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) due to multiple decoding rounds.
Proposes 'dSpark,' a schedule distillation method to improve generation speed.
Focuses on optimizing the commitment strategy—deciding when to commit to a token based on its predictive utility for future tokens.

stories.title: Game theory of academic effort and hiring in the age of AI
stories.author: Peter S. Park
bullet_points: AI is challenging traditional metrics of academic quality, such as the quality of research papers.
The accessibility of powerful AI tools has made producing 'strong theoretical results' cheaper.
This shift threatens the reliability of current academic signaling mechanisms used for hiring and evaluation.

stories.title: Auto-Research Arena: Benchmarking and Advancing Auto-Research in Language Modeling
stories.author: Hanwen Jiang
bullet_points: Introduces 'Auto-Research Arena,' a new multi-target benchmark for autonomous research systems.
The benchmark is designed to evaluate and advance the capabilities of AI systems performing research in language modeling.
It separates result qualification (admissibility based on quality/constraints) from actual research improvement.

stories.title: Learning Force-Reactive Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces FLORE, a new framework for learning force-reactive locomotion and manipulation in humanoids.
Addresses the complexity of tasks requiring coordinated contact force control across hands and body, which kinematics alone cannot solve.
Utilizes robot-free demonstrations captured via force-sensing grippers and wearable body trackers.

stories.title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
stories.author: Weiwen Liu
bullet_points: The research focuses on 'Work Agents,' which are evolving from simple information generators to systems capable of executing complex digital tasks.
The paper addresses a gap in current research by proposing a unified, work-centric, system-level perspective on how these agents operate.
Work agents are conceptualized as systems integrating foundation models with runtime harnesses to function within stateful workspaces.

stories.title: Information-Theoretic Secure Aggregation With Heterogeneous Client Quantization
stories.author: Itzhak Tamo
bullet_points: The paper addresses a challenge in Federated Learning (FL) regarding secure aggregation.
It tackles the issue of heterogeneous client quantization, where clients have different bandwidth constraints.
The research proposes a method for secure aggregation that accounts for varying quantization levels among clients.

stories.title: Does VGGT Know What It Does Not Know?
stories.author: David Nordström
bullet_points: The research investigates the uncertainty awareness of 3D reconstruction models like VGGT, which currently output deterministic predictions without error metrics.
The study tests if the model's internal features can implicitly signal when its pose estimation is incorrect, even if the model itself doesn't report uncertainty.
Using a linear probe on frozen VGGT features, the researchers successfully predicted pose failure on a challenging benchmark dataset (HardMatch) where the model failed 35% of the time.

stories.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Addresses the inefficiency of Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs) which require many decoding rounds for token generation.
Introduces 'dSpark,' a new schedule distillation method to improve generation speed by optimizing when to commit to token predictions.
Highlights that the utility of a token prediction depends not just on its predictability, but on how it aids in predicting subsequent, less predictable tokens.

stories.title: FOCUS: Active Critic Learning for Long-Horizon Language Model Agents
stories.author: Benjamin Van Durme
bullet_points: Introduces FOCUS, a new Reinforcement Learning (RL) method designed for long-horizon language model agents.
Addresses the challenge of sparse outcome rewards, where assigning credit to early actions is difficult.
Mitigates inaccuracies and high computational costs associated with learning value estimates for intermediate states using selective branching.

stories.title: Preserve to Expand: Source-Aware Adaptation and Model Merging for Multilingual LLM-Based ASR
stories.author: Ravi Shekhar
bullet_points: Addresses the challenge of expanding multilingual Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) systems to new languages.
Proposes using connector-based Speech LLMs where a trainable connector maps speech representations to a frozen LLM.
Investigates target-update construction and merging strategies to adapt the connector while preserving performance on previously supported languages.

stories.title: Learning When to Commit: Schedule Distillation for Fast Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Zhiqiang Shen
bullet_points: Introduces 'dSpark,' a new schedule distillation method for Diffusion Large Language Models (dLLMs).
Addresses the inefficiency of dLLMs, which require many decoding rounds despite parallel token generation.
Proposes that efficient generation depends on strategically committing to tokens that maximize future predictability, not just easy ones.

stories.title: Quantifying Claim Smoothing by LLM Research Agents
stories.author: Greg Durrett
bullet_points: LLMs used for deep research often produce confident-sounding reports that are factually inaccurate.
The phenomenon, termed 'claim smoothing,' describes how LLMs synthesize diverse sources into a single, overly smooth narrative.
This smoothing process causes the model to discard crucial evidential conflicts and 'jaggedness' present in the source material.

stories.title: SEMA-Auto: Sighted and Efficient Multi-Turn Attack with Autonomy
stories.author: Jianfeng Gao
bullet_points: Introduces SEMA-Auto, a new approach to multi-turn adversarial attacks (jailbreaking) against LLMs.
Addresses limitations of existing methods: static planners lack context, while interactive generators are computationally expensive due to required in-loop evaluators.
SEMA-Auto aims to bridge this gap by providing a 'sighted and efficient' mechanism for dynamic attack generation.

stories.title: Can JEV Support Clinical Trial Criteria Assessment?
stories.author: Wu Yuan
bullet_points: The research investigates using JEV, a non-generative decision model, for clinical trial prescreening.
The model is compared against schema-constrained Qwen Flash for distinguishing unmet conditions from insufficient evidence in patient records.
Evaluation was conducted on 2,048 test pairs using datasets derived from MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV under strict data retention protocols.

stories.title: Quantitative Generalization Bounds for Multi-Layer Transformers: A Few Long Strings can Beat Many Short Ones
stories.author: Michael Hahn
bullet_points: The paper addresses the theoretical understanding of transformer model generalization, which currently lags behind empirical observations.
It proposes quantitative generalization bounds for multi-layer transformers, focusing on how they handle complex inputs.
The research suggests that a few long training examples can outperform many short ones in terms of generalization ability.

stories.title: From Self-Confidence to Statistical Accuracy: Scaling Human-in-the-Loop Evaluation with Direct and LLM-Assisted Auditing
stories.author: Yang Zhou
bullet_points: Addresses the miscalibration issue of self-confidence scores reported by LLMs and MLLMs.
Proposes a unified statistical framework to improve evaluation methods for LLMs.
Compares and refines the use of direct human auditing versus LLM-as-a-judge for scalable model evaluation.

stories.title: Survival LLM: AI assistant and emergency library that runs on your own computer
stories.author: Luc
bullet_points: Introduction of 'Survival LLM,' an AI assistant designed to run locally on a user's own computer.
The core value proposition is providing an AI solution that does not rely on external cloud services.
It functions as both an AI assistant and an 'emergency library,' suggesting offline utility.
